#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.

An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.

A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.

The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).

Every write takes a lock (flock on .record.lock beside the record), checks the
state it would leave, appends the history blocks first and then replaces each
record file in one step. A write is refused only for what would break the
store: a bad number, a pointer that does not resolve or whose words do not
open its target's title, a line break in an entry, no provenance (neither
`--from` nor `--note`). Never for size. The tool does not commit: commit the
record file and its history together.

usage: record.py COMMAND [ARGS] [PROVENANCE] [--root DIR]

  PROVENANCE: --from PATH#HEADING (repeatable; PATH from the repository root
  or from explorations/, HEADING held by exactly one heading of it, as doc:
  resolves one), --commit HASH (in HEAD's history), --by WHO, --note WHY.
  Each write needs --from or --note.

  add F|P --section TITLE FILE   a new entry from FILE's one line, numbered
      record.py add F --section 'Landed semantics' new.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The fix' --by coordinator
  set N [FILE] [--section TITLE] entry N rewritten from FILE's line, or moved
      record.py set F-87 f87.md --from 'compile-ladder/rung-x/REPORT.md#The question' --note 'cut to the form'
  merge N --into M [FILE]        N removed, M rewritten from FILE (or kept),
                                 every pointer to N made a pointer to M
      record.py merge F-90 --into F-87 f87.md --note 'one fact, two entries'
  remove N                       N removed; refused while a pointer to it remains
      record.py remove P-131 --note 'evicted to the coordinator skill, references/briefing.md'
  apply FILE                     many changes from one file, all or none (below)
      record.py apply chunk3.md --by 'consolidation chunk 3'
  check [--base COMMIT]          the store's checks; exit 1 on a failure
      record.py check --base cc9424c2a

An apply file holds, in any order: `## TITLE` or `### TITLE`, the section the
new entries below it go to (an existing entry stands under no heading, or
under its own section's, or the `## ` one that holds it); entry lines as they
should stand, `- F-87 ...`, or `- F-?1 ...` for a new entry, its placeholder
replaced by its number everywhere in the file; `move F-87 to SECTION`;
`remove F-90`; `merge F-91 into F-87`. Each may be followed by one indented
provenance line of its own:
`  from: PATH, "HEADING"; commit: HASH; by: WHO; note: WHY`. Blank lines and
`<!-- -->` comments are ignored. An entry line equal to the entry is skipped.

check fails on: an entry line without its number, or a line under an entry
that continues it; a number on two lines; a number with no `numbered` or
`added` block, or one gone from its file whose last block is not `merged into`
or `removed`; a pointer to no live entry, or quoted words that do not open the
target's title; with --base, an entry at COMMIT that is neither its line now
nor the earlier line of a block in its history (pointer words refreshed by the
tool aside). It reports, without failing: the entries over 600 characters, the
entries without a bold title, and the `--from` paths and the report sections
an entry cites (`PATH`, "HEADING") that do not resolve.

The reads are facts-extract.sh's: `F-87`, `F-87+` (with the entries it points
to and that point to it), `history:F-87`, and the title queries, which fall

## 2. Your questions, in the order they block the batch

### Q1. May the checker refuse an object that inherits an abstract method from one trait and its body from another (rows 572 and 727; review-queue item 62)?

**The question in plain words.** A functional method is declared with `self` among its parameters and called `pick(x)`. A trait may leave one abstract, with no body. Take:

```
trait A  pick(self): String  end           (* abstract *)
trait B  pick(self): String = "b"  end     (* a body *)
object O extends { A, B } end              (* declares no pick of its own *)
```

`pick(O)` has two candidates, `A`'s and `B`'s, and neither is more specific. The specification refuses `O` twice: an object must define each abstract method it inherits (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:628-633`), and a type that provides two such declarations must provide one on their meet (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`, "Meet Rule"; "provides" includes abstract declarations, `traits.tex:580-581`). Today the compiled path accepts `O` and runs `B`'s body, also for a call typed by `A`; walk refuses `O` at load, by its per-provider Meet check (F-142; row 572). The cause is one filter: in a component the checker reads no abstract functional method of a trait the component declares (`OverloadingChecker.scala:138-141`), while it reads abstract dotted methods (`:183-193`), where it refuses the same shape written `o.m()`. The same filter lets a trait declare `f(self, y: S): ZZ32` abstract beside `f(self, y: S): ZZ32 = 2`, two identical declarations, and the code generator then crashes on them (row 727).

**Why it comes to you.** Climb batch 8's judge chose not to read those declarations (its decision 1, way (b)), and that default is on your review list as item 62, "default left with the row". Reading them, the judge's way (a), refuses both shapes. The sources split: the specification, the type group's rules (P-26) and the team's own dotted check refuse; the team's own abstract-method check accepts, counting a body `O` inherits as the implementation (`AbstractMethodChecker.scala:94-107`, the team's lines), so the team's two checks part by the shape; Java refuses `O` too ("inherits abstract and default"); Scala accepts it, a concrete member implementing an abstract one from any trait. For row 727's single-trait shape the specification, Java and Scala refuse a method declared twice; the type group's Welterweight calculus admits an abstract and a concrete declaration at one domain (`No-Dup-Abs-Conc`, `Papers/Types/fig-meetrule.tick:14`), which P-149 does not take.

**The ways.** (a) The checker reads them, keeping today's rule that an abstract declaration implemented by a subtype's body with the same parameter types is not checked against it; rows 727 and 572 close, the code generator's crash becomes the checker's refusal. (b) Leave them unread, item 62's default; the rows stay. Item 62's other way, an abstract-method check that demands the object's own declaration, refuses row 572 only.

**Answered at 06:23 UTC on 2026-10-15: (a), refuse (P-149), and rung K builds it.** Walk refuses both rows' shapes at load and the library loads, and the Q1 probe found no type in the one library or the compiler's library that inherits an abstract functional method and a sibling's body without their meet (`explorations/perf-probes/abstract-sibling-body/REPORT.md`). K holds the line and reports if the library or the compiler's own library is refused.

Each is settled by the record's principles and is reversible; none reverses a decision of yours. Calls 1 to 3 are the coordinator's calls of climb batch 15b, now built; calls 4 to 6 are drafted here for its confirmation.

1. **Q2 of the checker-speed probe is built as its own rung, S** (PLAN, "Climb batch 15b, listed for his review"). P-148 puts the checker's speed right after its correctness; S changes no result, which its tables, the checker's whole output and an audit of every reused answer show. The way, a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers or fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold, is the rung's, by its profile. The precedent for a shared memo is the tree's own: row 688's ground memo shares an answer that read no context across every analyzer over one trait table (`TraitTable.scala:100-115`).

Splitting today's few waits for a profile that shows them costing anything (section 4).
3. **Q3 of the probe is built, rung H: a node's hash no longer depends on the JVM's identity hashes.** The team gave the nodes' base class a counter for its hash, "a more deterministic replay than Object.hashCode()" (`nodes_util/UIDObject.java:26-34`); the revival already post-processes the generated nodes so that a rebuild writes them byte for byte (`build.xml:667-677`); javac and scalac aim at the same output from the same input, the reproducible-builds practice. The specification is silent on where; javac and scalac report a bound violation at the type argument's use. By reading two sites of the distance move to their calls (`:3405` to `:3422`, `:3411` to `:3424`, row 433's).

## 3. The rungs

### The rule the rungs keep, and how they meet

- No two rungs change one declaration, and no rung builds on another rung of the same batch (PLAN, "The principle for the batches"). S is the solver: TypeAnalyzer's meets, normal form and memos, TraitTable's memo, Formula's fold and reduction. H is the syntax tree's hash lines, their generators and build.xml's makeAST. K is the overloading check's per-provider set and the well-formedness walk. W is walk's generic pair check, if and big-operator hint.

## 4. What the batch leaves out, each with its home
### What every agent of the run reads first

This run is climb batch 16, the record CLIMB-BATCH-16.md, phase 3's next batch after climb batch 15b, toward the checker at a true zero. No site of the distance is free to fix: every one waits on a decision of the curator, a language feature not built or a checker project. So the batch makes the checker faster and its output fixed, and repairs rows outside the distance: one rung on the checker's solver with a guard on the build's long methods (the checker-speed probe's Q2 and its skeptic's guard, the coordinator's calls), one on the syntax tree's hashes (Q3, the coordinator's call), one checker rung on a component's abstract functional methods and a broken bound's error place (rows 727, 572 and 720, by Q1's answer), and one walk rung on its generic overload check at load, its if and a user big operator's result (rows 373, 673 and 718). The distance stands at 49 and the count at 39 after climb batch 15b (compile-ladder/climb-batch-15b/gate/), the count stage 325 s at its gate. The rungs meet only in a measure: no two rungs change one declaration, and no rung builds on another. **The compiled checker reduces a formula once in each analyzer, answers an exclusion asked again with fresh inference variables from a memo, and finds a type by its name once per trait table.**

- `Formula.reduce` asks `TypeAnalyzer.reduced`, which keeps each analyzer's reductions by formula, each marked if it read the context, and keeps none that opened a size (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:589-609`; switch `fortress.analyzer.reduce.cache`).
- `dExc` keeps its answers by the question with its type inference variables renamed apart, from an empty cycle history only (`:408-439`, `:985-1015`; switch `fortress.analyzer.exclusion.cache`). Those that read no context are shared through the trait table (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:150-156`).
- `TraitTable.typeCons` and `declaredTypeCons` answer once per name (`TraitTable.scala:34-68`; switch `fortress.analyzer.typecons.cache`).

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

11	## 1. What changed and why
12	
13	Commits on `wip/rung-solver-speed`, cut from `528438ac5`:
14	
15	| commit | what |
16	|---|---|
17	| `aaac79b84` | tests: `ReductionMemoJUTest` (red on the base) and the guard `MethodSizeJUTest` |
18	| `615ecff76` | the change: `Formula.reduce` asks the analyzer for a reduction it made before (`TypeAnalyzer.reduced`) |
19	| `60d8081ea` | tests: `ExclusionMemoJUTest` and `TraitTableMemoJUTest` (red on the change) |
20	| `6e6192747` | the second pass: the exclusion memo by renamed question, and the table's two lookups |
21	
22	**The change.** `Formula.reduce` simplifies a conjunction or a disjunction. For each inference variable it meets the upper bounds and joins the lower bounds, then tests them for contradiction and redundancy, each test a subtype or exclusion question (`Formula.scala:365-466`).
23	
24	- `Formula.and` and `or` reduce after every step of their fold. `implies`, `isTrue`, `isFalse` and `equivalent` reduce both sides, and `maximalCFormulas` reduces each pair.
25	- So the same formula is reduced again and again: 35,107,747 reductions over the component, 34,447,211 of them of a formula already in reduced form (section 4).
26	
27	Now `reduce` sends an `And` or an `Or` to `TypeAnalyzer.reduced` (`Formula.scala:360-363`), which keeps each analyzer's answers (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:589-609`):
28	
29	- **The key is the formula.** A reduction asks only the analyzer's public questions (`meet`, `join`, `subtype`, `excludes`, `lteq`, `definitelyExcludes`), each from an empty cycle history. So its answer depends on the formula and on the analyzer's trait table and kind environment, and the analyzer owns the memo. The negation flag takes no part: no reduction is asked under a negation.
30	- **Context reads.** An answer whose computation read the context (`traits.contextReads` moved) is marked, and a hit on it is a context read too (`traits.readContext()`). So an enclosing computation is never shared by the ground memo as context-free. This is the normalize memos' rule (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:616-620`).
31	- **Opened sizes.** A reduction that opened a size (`Formula.openedSizeCount` moved, `Formula.scala:150`) is not kept: computed again, it would open a fresh size with another name.
32	- **The switch** is `fortress.analyzer.reduce.cache`, default on, beside the analyzer's other switches.
33	
34	**The second pass.** After the change, the profile held `TypeAnalyzer.dExc` at 62.7 % inclusive, from `normConjunct`'s pair test `x.exists(y => x.exists(z => dExc(y, z)))` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:768`). It also held the trait table's walk of every type it holds: `TraitTable.find` at `pSubInner`'s declaration search 11.9 %, `TraitTable.typeCons` 6.6 % (section 5). The pass takes all three:
35	
36	- **The exclusion memo.** `dExc` keeps its answers by the question with its type inference variables renamed apart (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:408-439`; `renamedApart`, `:985-1015`).
37	  - An inference call makes fresh variables, so `Number` against `MultiplicativeRing[\$i\]` was asked with a new `$i` each time and never met a memo.
38	  - The answer is a Boolean, and it is the same under every renaming of the variables, because the computation compares them only by equality.
39	  - It is kept only from an empty cycle history and marked if its computation read the context. If it read none, it is shared through the trait table (`TraitTable.scala:150-156`), as the ground memo shares its answers. It is not kept if the computation opened a size.
40	  - A question that holds a size or operator inference variable is not kept.
41	  - The renamed variables hash by their number, so a renaming asks the JVM for no identity hash.
42	  - The switch is `fortress.analyzer.exclusion.cache`.
43	- **`TraitTable.typeCons`** keeps its answer by the name's api and text (`TraitTable.scala:34-53`). An `Id`'s span takes no part in a lookup, since `SpanInfo.equals` is true of any two spans. The indices' maps of types are built once (`CollectUtil.immutable`, `compiler/index/CompilationUnitIndex.java:41`).
44	- **The declaration search.** `pSubInner` searched for a trait's declaration by its text, walking every type of the table for every comparison of two instances of one generic trait (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:271` at 528438ac5). It is now `traits.declaredTypeCons(text)` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:267`; `TraitTable.scala:55-66`): the same walk, once per name. The table's walk meets its types in the same order each time, while the table holds the same types.
45	- Both lookups share the switch `fortress.analyzer.typecons.cache`.
46	
47	**The guard.** `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/MethodSizeJUTest.java`, in the misc track, reads every class under `ProjectFortress/build` with `java.lang.classfile`, as `WalkerJUTest` reads `Walker` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/nodes/WalkerJUTest.java:59-76`).
48	
49	- It fails on any method over 8,000 bytes of bytecode that its list does not name, and names each such method with its size.
50	- It also fails on a listed method that is gone from the build or back under the limit, so that the list stays true.
51	- `WalkerJUTest` is as it was. The list is in section 8.

# Rung H (rung-ast-hashes): the record lines

## FACTS

- **The syntax tree's hashes do not depend on the JVM's identity hashes; one checker site still does.**
  - Every generated node's hash starts from the hash of its class's name. makeAST's post-processing of ASTGen's output and the in-repo generators write it (`build.xml:679-697`).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                appends TEXT to row N's notes
  close N --commit HASH --test NAME [--note TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C]
        [--spec C] [--found-by C]
                             after the fix has landed: HASH must be in HEAD's
                             history and NAME a test under the test folders;
                             writes the one-line FIXED row (the claim's first
                             sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed
                             HASH; full text: history, row N`); the options
                             give cells the old row lacks in the template's form
  duplicate N --of M [--add TEXT] [--claim C] [--class C] [--spec C]
        [--reproducer C] [--found-by C]
                             makes row N a DUPLICATE pointer to row M (notes
                             `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`);
                             --add appends TEXT to row M's notes
  check [--rows FILE] [--base COMMIT] [--summary]
                             lints every row against the template, and the
                             tables' headers, numbers and order; --rows lints
                             a file holding only row lines instead; --base
                             also checks that every row at COMMIT is the same
                             line now or has its full earlier line in the
                             history file, and that the set of row numbers is

<!-- Climb batch 16, rung H (rung-ast-hashes): the syntax tree's hashes apart from the JVM's identity hashes, by the coordinator's call on Q3 of the checker-speed probe; row 488; F-232. Worktree /home/user/fortress-asthashes, branch wip/rung-ast-hashes, base 528438ac5. -->

# Rung H: the syntax tree's hashes apart from the JVM's identity hashes

- problem: the checker-speed probe's H runs. One extra identity hash reordered the api checks and printed three unions the other way (`explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:327-353`; F-232).
- spec: none. `grep -rn -i hash Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` finds only the commented-out `hashCode` and `hash` of `Object` in `Specification/basic-lib/objects.tex:25-32`. Those are about Fortress objects, not the implementation's syntax tree.
- precedent: the makeAST target's normalization of ASTGen's timestamp by a `replaceregexp` (`build.xml:668-678`, `3c4dcdabc`); the team's counter hash for the nodes' base class, "a more deterministic replay than Object.hashCode()" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/UIDObject.java:28-34`); the PLT `Wrapper`'s own formula, its value's hash XOR its class's hash, for `NodeHash` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java:24-36`).
- deviation: an Option-typed field's hash goes through a new helper, `NodeHash.of`, in a file the brief does not list (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java:18`). The PLT Option classes hash by identity hashes. A second `replaceregexp` writes the call (`build.xml:693-697`).
- deviation: the generated javadoc above each `generateHashCode` still says "the hashcode of the class object" (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/TraitType.java:99-102`). It comes from ASTGen's template and the three generators, and I left it as it was.
- deviation: `TransformationNode`'s line changes too, though no class is generated from it. `TransformationNodeCreator` builds the 241 `_SyntaxTransformation` classes as ASTGen `NodeClass`es (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/TransformationNodeCreator.java:79-80`). So 454 classes have the line from ASTGen's template and 482 from `TemplateGapClass` and `EllipsesNode`, not 213 and 723.
- historical: `build.xml`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/EllipsesNode.java:195`, `astgen/TemplateGapClass.java:204`, `astgen/TransformationNode.java:190`, the 18 files of `parser_util/precedence_opexpr/` (for example `RealExpr.java:117`), `useful/Cons.java:112`, `useful/Empty.java:86`, `interpreter/evaluator/_WrappedFValue.java:171`. The 936 regenerated files of `nodes/` were not in the 2012 tree (`git ls-tree a874948ac -- ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/` lists none).

## 1. What changed and why

Every hash map and set of syntax tree nodes iterated in an order set by the JVM's identity-hash sequence, for two reasons:

1. Every generated node's `generateHashCode` started from `getClass().hashCode()`, the `Class` object's identity hash (`nodes/TraitType.java:104` at the base). There were 936 such classes, and the same line was in 21 hand-written classes.
2. A field whose type holds a PLT `Option` was hashed by the Option's own `hashCode`, and both Option classes hash by identity hashes:
   - `edu.rice.cs.plt.tuple.Null.generateHashCode` is `System.identityHashCode(this)`;
   - `Wrapper.generateHashCode` XORs its value's hash with `getClass().hashCode()` (`javap -c -p -cp ProjectFortress/third_party/plt/plt.jar edu.rice.cs.plt.tuple.Null`, `... Wrapper`).

   Every `Id` holds an `Option<APIName>` and every `TypeInfo` an `Option<WhereClause>`, so nearly every node reaches one. 190 field hashes in 131 classes are of this kind: 171 `Option<Node>`, 13 `Option<List<...>>`, 4 `List<Option<CoercionInvocation>>` and 2 `Option<Option<CoercionInvocation>>`.

The change:
- `build.xml:679-697`. After the timestamp's normalization, the makeAST target makes two rewrites:
  - `int code = getClass().hashCode();` becomes `int code = getClass().getName().hashCode();`. `String.hashCode` is fixed by its definition, so the class name's hash is the same in every JVM.
  - `code ^= temp_f.hashCode();` becomes `code ^= NodeHash.of(temp_f);` wherever the line above declares `temp_f` with a type that holds `Option<`.
- `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeHash.java`. `of(field)` hashes:
  - an empty Option as the hash of `Null`'s class name;
  - a full one as its value's `of` XOR the hash of `Wrapper`'s class name;
  - a list by its elements' `of`, as `List.hashCode` does;
  - anything else by its own `hashCode`.

  Two equal Options have equal `of`: `Null` is one object, and `Wrapper.equals` compares the class and the value.
- The three in-repo generators write the class name's hash directly (`astgen/EllipsesNode.java:195`, `astgen/TemplateGapClass.java:204`, `astgen/TransformationNode.java:190`). Their own fields hold no Option.
- The 936 nodes are checked in as the build writes them: 936 lines `getClass().getName().hashCode()` and 190 lines `NodeHash.of` (`git diff 528438ac5 HEAD -- ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/ | grep '^[-+] '`, 1,126 lines each way).
- The hand-written classes with the line:
  - the 18 classes of `parser_util/precedence_opexpr/`, checked in with no generator in the build;
  - `useful/Cons.java:112` and `useful/Empty.java:86`;
  - `interpreter/evaluator/_WrappedFValue.java:171`, which still XORs its `FValue`'s hash, walk's own (row 430); only its class part changes.

What stays: `_InferenceVarType`, `_InferenceVarOp` and `_InferenceVarInt` keep a bare `Object` as their id (`nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1166-1184`), so their hashes stay identity hashes. Section 4.4 shows that no output of the count stage moves through them, so the brief's condition for changing them is not met.

Commits:
- `9ec2fbe0f`: the test.
- `0f8dfe9a6`: the change (962 files).
- `5bb043630`: the `XXX` test of section 5. It adds test files only, so the tree's code is `0f8dfe9a6`'s.

## 5. Defects and their homes

- **The nodes' hashes moved with the identity-hash sequence (F-232).** Home 1: this change repairs it, and `NodeHashJUTest` asserts it.
- **A component's function without a return type takes the return type of the api's first declaration of its name, in identity-hash order (NEW-H-1).** Home 2: the specification settles it.
  - The component is expanded so that each construct "corresponding to declarations in APIs exported by $C$" includes "all types ... included in the exported APIs" (`Specification/basic/components/type-inference.tex`, section "Type Inference for Components", step 1). The corresponding declaration is the one that the function satisfies, of its own parameter type (`basic/components/source-code.tex`, the satisfaction of a top-level function declaration).
  - The gated `XXX` test is `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi.test`. Its api declares `pick(): ZZ32` and `pick(x: String): String`, and its component `pick() = 1` and `pick(x: String) = x`. Whichever declaration comes first, the other body fails its borrowed type, so the test fails in every order. Compiled path only: walk checks no types.
  - As it is, on the base's code: `explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base16 $PWD/tmp/old-caches junit $PWD/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi.test` prints `Function body has type IntLiteral, but declared return type is String.`, ` Saw expected failure`, `OK (1 test)`.
  - With the defect removed for one run (both declarations given their return types), then restored: ` Saw failure, but did not satisfy compile_err_contains; expected`, `Saw wrong failure. compile`, `FAILURES!!!`, `Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0`.
  - On the change: `ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh xxxnew ProjectFortress/compiler_tests XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi.test` prints ` Saw expected failure`, `OK (1 test)`. In `ant testFast` it is one of the compiler track's 1,213, all passing.
- **Row 488's `:130`.** Its mechanism is NEW-H-1 (section 4.3). The row stays open, with a note: the H runs still move it.
- **Inference variables' ids are identity hashes** (`nodes_util/NodeFactory.java:1166-1184`). I measured that they reach no output (section 4.4). No program shows it, so it needs no home beyond this report.

## 6. Old against new

| program | old (base build) | new | same? |
|---|---|---|---|
| the count stage on the one library | 382 s; 39 / 38 | 395 s and 376 s; 39 / 38 | the table yes; the output up to the api order and three unions |
| the H-run driver, N = 0, 1, 1000 | the probe's runs: three api orders; the unions moved in three messages at N = 1 and in one at N = 1000 | one order, one union spelling; `:130` absent at N = 0 only | section 4.2 |
| the node-hashing copy | api order, `:130` and two unions move | nothing moves | section 4.4 |
| the distance stage | 49 (climb batch 15b's gate) | 48 | `:130` gone, `:1463`'s union reversed (section 7) |
| `XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi` | expected failure | expected failure | yes |
| `NodeHashJUTest` | red | green | changed, as meant |

## 7. The checker count and the distance

**The count.** The after is the pass run on the final code (`tmp/count/pass.txt`, copied to `tmp/rung-ast-hashes/checker-count-postedit.txt`). Against the last landed gate's table, `diff explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-15b/gate/checker-count.txt tmp/rung-ast-hashes/checker-count-postedit.txt` prints nothing.

**The distance.** `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/rung-ast-hashes/distance-postedit.txt tmp/rung-ast-hashes/dist-post` took 1,233 s: load at start 2.19, with testFast beside it.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-15b/gate/distance.txt tmp/rung-ast-hashes/distance-postedit.txt
    DISTANCE DOWN   49 -> 48 (-1)
        kind typecheck               40 -> 39     (-1)
        class BR                      4 -> 3      (-1)  big operators: a reduction's body typed as the element, not the BigReduction or Comprehension declared
        unit component FortressLibrary     43 -> 42     (-1)

The sites, by row: `tmp/rung-ast-hashes/dist-post/errors.tsv` against `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, tree paths masked, sorted, diffed.
- **Gone:** `FortressLibrary.fss:130`, "Function body has type TotalComparison, but declared return type is BigReduction[\TotalComparison,TotalComparison\]." This is row 488's site, through NEW-H-1: the distance stage's own identity-hash sequence now puts the generator overload first. It is not a repair. Any edit that moves the sequence can bring it back, and the count stage on this same tree keeps it.
- **One row gone and one come at one site:** `FortressLibrary.fss:1463`, `OR(O0,I0)` became `OR(I0,O0)`.
- **Unchanged:** `:3367` and `:3384` print `OR(IntLiteral,T)` in both lists.

No other row moved. No library line moved, so row 577's misattribution does not arise.

## 8. The suites

These ran after the last change of code (`0f8dfe9a6`; the tree at `5bb043630`):

    ant testFast        BUILD SUCCESSFUL   Total time: 16 minutes 21 seconds
      compiler      1213 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors   (1212 at climb batch 15b's gate, plus XXXOmittedReturnTypeFromApi)
      library         86, 0, 0;   othercompiler 263, 0, 0
      misc           428, 0, 0   (427 at the gate, plus NodeHashJUTest)
      ASTJUTest 13/0, NodeFactoryJUTest 1/0, WalkerJUTest 4/0, NodeHashJUTest 1/0
    ant testSystem      BUILD SUCCESSFUL   Total time: 6 minutes 5 seconds
      system-0 149, system-1 161, system-2 150, system-3 161: 621 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors (621 at the gate)
    ant testSpecData    [junit] Tests run: 130, Failures: 0, Errors: 0   BUILD SUCCESSFUL   Total time: 49 seconds

No verdict changed. The loads were high: rung K's runs and the distance stage ran beside them.

## 9. The ladder subset

The subset is all 85 programs of the baseline's pass list and the 18 microGPT components, because every node's hash changes. The drivers are copied under `tmp/rung-ast-hashes/ladder/` as `gate.md` says, with the caches copied after the library order.

# Rung K: abstract functional methods read, a broken bound reported at the call

- problem: on the base `XXXNoDuplicatesRuleAbstract` was keyed on the code generator's stop, 'Likely bug in static analysis, apparently malformed overload set not rejected' (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:409-411`). The per-provider set dropped a component's own bodiless functional method (`OverloadingChecker.scala:138-141` at 528438ac5). Row 720's reproducer named the callee's result, not the call: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/OverloadSet.java:411`
- spec: a trait provides what it declares or inherits, abstract declarations included (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:580-581`), and an object must define each abstract method it inherits: `Specification/basic/traits.tex:628-633`
- precedent: the team's dotted per-provider set keeps abstract dotted methods with no body filter: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:170-172`
- deviation: the team's 2012 functional set kept bodies only (a874948ac, line 133); it now keeps every functional method a type provides: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:137`
- deviation: the well-formedness walk's own `error` now chooses the error's place, with three helpers beside it and two lines of `walk`: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:42-82`
- historical: OverloadingChecker.scala, TypeWellFormedChecker.scala and `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, all of the 2012 tree: `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2622`

For where a static error is reported, the specification says nothing: `grep -rn -i 'reported at\|is reported\|location of .*error' Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` prints nothing.

## 1. What changed, and why

**Rows 727, 572 and 734: the per-provider check reads abstract functional methods.** Q1's answer is (a), refuse (P-149). `toFunctionalMethodArrows` now keeps every functional method a trait or object provides, as `toMethodArrows` keeps every dotted one (`OverloadingChecker.scala:131-137`). It keeps the `implemented` filter, which drops an abstract method that a declaration of a strict subtype with the same parameter types implements (`:147-152`). Before, in a component, it kept a functional method only if the method had a body or its trait came from an imported api (`:138-141` at the base). That was the judge's reading (b) of climb batch 8 (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-overloading-checker/JUDGE.md`, section 7, decision 1). The revival's helper `declaredInUnit`, used only by that condition, is removed (`:173-181` at the base).
- Row 727: an abstract `f(self, y: S)` beside a concrete `f(self, y: S)` in one trait is refused, 'There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type: (S)'. So is the pair at two self positions, through row 707's check.
- Row 572: in `object O extends { A, B }`, `A` has an abstract `pick(self)` and `B` a concrete one. The object is refused, 'Invalid overloading of pick in trait O: A->String ... and B->String ...', as its dotted twin already was.
- Row 734, the Q1 probe's row of the same shape with return types that differ, is refused the same way.
- One more face, measured here. On the base, an object's own `f(self): String` that defines its trait's abstract `f(self): ZZ32` compiled, and its run failed with 'java.lang.VerifyError: Bad return type'. The dotted twin was refused. The return-type check of an overriding pair reads its arrows through the same function (`OverloadingChecker.scala:657-658`), so it now refuses the functional one too: 'For f, the return type of O->String ... should be a subtype of the return type of T->ZZ32'.
- Operators stay as row 584 leaves them: `isDeclaredName` and `NodeUtil.validOp` are untouched (`OverloadingChecker.scala:710-714`). A symbolic operator's pair, row 726, is still the code generator's stop.

**Row 720: a broken bound is reported at the call.** A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type. The well-formedness walk meets that type in the call's type information, and on the base it reported the error at the type node (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:158-165` at the base), which is the callee's declaration. The walk now remembers the nearest expression it is in (`:65`, `:145-146`, `:274`).
- An error on a type node that lies outside that expression is reported at the expression instead (`:47-62`, `:72-82`).
- It is reported once for each message and place of the node, as the errors at the node were. The driver drops a second error with the same text and place (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/MultipleStaticError.java:31-40`).
- It goes to the innermost expression the walk met the node in, and to the first of them where two are disjoint.
- It is not moved when the node is ill-formed where it is written: then the error stays at the declaration, as before.
- A type written inside its own expression, a parameter's type and a declaration's type keep their errors where they were.

Two earlier versions were wrong, and each fault has a test now:
- The first (96c441771) reported at the nearest expression each time. `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` printed 'has 3 errors' on it, against 1 on the base: a call in a tuple, the tuple, and a second call of the callee.
- The second (f53bee311) also moved the error of a type that is ill-formed where it is written, so that error came twice. `GenTest5` went from 32 errors to 42, and `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce` printed 'has 2 errors'.
- The third (a79a51661) gives the base's number of errors in every program I compared.

## 2. The test before the fix, and after
## 7. Sentences made false

- The Effect of "Overloading with static parameters", `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2622-2627` at the base: "and reads no abstract functional method of a trait that the component it checks declares (row~727): two declarations of such an operator, or such an abstract method and a concrete one, with the same parameter type pass it, and only its code generator refuses them, as a malformed overload set (rows~726 and~727)." It is corrected here (`changes.tex:2622-2629`), in two sentences. The first says the checker reads the abstract functional methods a type provides as it reads abstract dotted ones, and refuses the pair that only its code generator refused before. The second keeps the operator half (rows 584 and 726).
- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2630-2633` (now), "The interpreter loads such a pair ... (row~373)", is made false by rung W, not by this rung. It is left for the gather.
- No other sentence of `Specification/` or `Documentation/` says what the checker does with abstract functional methods or where it reports a bound. `grep -rn 'row~727\|row~572\|row~720\|row~734\|malformed overload' Specification Documentation` finds only the corrected Effect.
- The specification builds clean: `./ant genSource` and `./ant tex` end 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL', and the log has no 'LaTeX Warning: Reference', multiply-defined label or undefined control sequence.
- These statements in the record are false now, which is revival-change material:
  - F-80's "Unchecked: a pair one of whose declarations is the component's own abstract one (row 572)";
  - F-223's "and reads no abstract functional method of a trait the component declares (row 727); such a pair passes it and stops the code generator (rows 726 and 727)", and its naming of `XXXNoDuplicatesRuleAbstract` among the checker's departures;
  - row 572's walk note ('InterpreterBug ... row 100's mechanism'), already stale since F-142;
  - the places in rows 720 and 433;
  - JUDGE.md decision 1's reading (b), as the checker's behaviour.

## 8. Decisions, each with the ways not taken

1. **Rows 727 and 572: drop the body filter and keep `implemented`** (P-149, reading (a)). Not taken:
   - (b), the base's reading (JUDGE.md section 7);
   - Scala's exemption for a sibling body, the Q1 probe's `scala` shadows, which P-149 refuses;
   - a check in `AbstractMethodChecker` (item 62's other way), which the brief excludes and which would leave row 727 to the code generator.
2. **`declaredInUnit` is removed**, rather than left unused. The revival wrote it for the filter alone (70d5486f9), and nothing else calls it: `grep -rn declaredInUnit ProjectFortress/src` prints nothing now.
3. **Row 720 is fixed in the walk, by reporting at an enclosing expression.** The ways weighed:
   - (a) the nearest expression each time, the first version: errors multiplied;
   - (b) once per message and place, at the innermost expression, the second version: it doubled a type that is ill-formed where it is written;
   - (c) taken: (b), and no move where the node is ill-formed where it is written. This gives the base's number of errors, at the call;
   - (d) check a call's static arguments against the chosen callee's bounds in the type checker, at the call. It moves the check into `STypeChecker`'s call path, with rung S's solver underneath, and drops the walk's check of every other type in expression information;
   - (e) give a call's type the call's spans where the checker instantiates the declared type. That changes the spans every other message prints.
4. **`error` itself chooses the place**, so the errors of `getTypes` and `walkStaticArgs` follow the same rule. `error` is the walk's own helper (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:47`). Not taken: changing only the bound error's call (`:202-204`), which would leave the walk's other errors on a call's type at the callee.
5. **The key of a placed error is its message and the node's printed place**, the text the driver de-duplicates on (`MultipleStaticError.java:31-40`). So each of the base's distinct errors stays one error. Not taken: the node's identity, under which a type built twice from one declaration is reported twice.
6. **Two tests beyond the brief's list**, each for a defect measured here that the repair closes: row 734 (`XXXFunctionalMethodMeetAbstractSiblingNarrower`) and the return-type face (`XXXAbstractFunctionalMethodReturnType`). There is also one guard for each faulty earlier version.
7. **The dotted guard pins today's 'in trait O'** for an object, home 3 of NEW-K-1. Not taken: keying on 'Invalid overloading of m in' only.
8. **The speed pass makes no edit**: the profile gives the two declarations nothing to save (section 6). Not taken: a memo of a type's functional arrows across its providers. It would need an audit and saves nothing that can be measured.
9. **The base was timed a second time**, beside the same job as the pass, for a like-for-like pair. The run used private scratch; nothing else ran in the base build.
10. **The tests are compile tests with the `XXX` prefix**, the folder's convention for a refusal at compile time.

## 9. Points to report

- **A declaration of either library that the check now refuses: none.** Rows 727 and 572's line landed (96c441771). The compiler's library compiles in all five library-order runs. In the distance stage, no site of the one library comes or goes.
- **The messages now printed.**
  - Row 727: 'There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type: (S)', at `XXXNoDuplicatesRuleAbstract.fss:7:3-21` and `:8:3-25`.
  - Row 572: 'Invalid overloading of pick in trait O: A->String @ ...:7:3-8:1 and B->String @ ...:10:3-26'.
  - Row 720: 'Ill-formed type: V[\T\] The static argument T does not satisfy the corresponding bound K.', at `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCall.fss:13:19-27`, the call `vec[\T\]()`. The reproducer's two errors are at `FactoryUnboundedCaller.fss:16:20-17:8`.
- **Count or distance sites beyond :3405 and :3411: none.** Those two moved to :3422 and :3424.

<!-- Climb batch 16, rung K's judge: the ruling on the skeptic's contested fix 491a5631a (each call whose static argument breaks the callee's bound is reported at its own place), upheld; the rung stands. -->

# Rung K (`rung-checker-abstract-callsite`): the judge's ruling on its contested fix

Written 2026-10-16 by the batch's judge (Opus), on `wip/rung-checker-abstract-callsite` at `587097d58`. Nothing was built or run for it. Every point is a reading of the tree at that commit, of the worker's last code commit `a79a51661`, or of a result that the worker's `REPORT.md` or the skeptic's `SKEPTIC.md` quotes with its command.

## 1. Ruling

**`491a5631a` is upheld, and nothing is reverted. Decision: stands.** The rung lands as the branch holds it.

The skeptic contested one fix. The finding is right, and so is its way. The worker's key dropped the error of a call whose static argument breaks the bound whenever another call of the same callee, in any declaration, printed the same message. The coordinator's call 4 asks for every such call to be reported at the call. The fix reports each one, and keeps the guards that the worker built against extra errors.

## 2. What the fix changes

At `a79a51661`, a moved error was keyed on its message and on the place of the node, `n.at` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:48` at `a79a51661`). Only one error was kept per key (`:55-59` there). A second place that did not lie inside the first fell to `case _ =>` at `:59`, and was not reported.

A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type (ledger row 720). So for two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike, `n.at` is the same: the callee's result type. The two calls therefore had one key and one error.

At `491a5631a`, a moved error is kept for each type node met, at the innermost expression that the walk met that node in (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:75-85`). The errors are made at the end of `check` (`:41-58`):
- If one place of a key lies strictly inside another place of the same key, the outer place gives no error (`:50-56`).
- A key that the walk also met where its node is written gives no moved error at all (`:44`, `:72-74`).

## 3. Why it is upheld

1. **Call 4 settles the place, and it settles it for each call.** Call 4 says "a static argument that breaks the callee's bound is reported at the call" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84`), and the rung's section repeats it as "an error is reported at the call whose static argument breaks the bound" (`:176`).
   - The second call in `SkTwoCalls` is such a call. So is `again`'s call in the worker's own `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss:14`).
   - At `a79a51661` neither got any error. The skeptic's run (`SKEPTIC.md` section 5.2):

         tmp/.../skeptic/bin/diffrun.sh SkTwoCalls SkTwoCallsU
         SkTwoCalls.fss:9:21-29:           ... File SkTwoCalls.fss has 1 error.
         SkTwoCallsU.fss:9:21-29:  SkTwoCallsU.fss:10:22-30:  ... File SkTwoCallsU.fss has 2 errors.

   - The worker's test asserted the drop. At `a79a51661`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test` held `compile_err_WIcontains=File XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.fss has 1 error.` (the minus line of `git show 491a5631a`).
   - Call 4's precedent is javac and scalac, which report a bound violation at each use of the type argument (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:84`). That is one error for each call, not one for each declaration.
   - The specification says nothing about where an error is reported (`REPORT.md`, its grep under the provenance lines). So nothing outweighs call 4 here.

2. **The worker's precedent, read exactly, gives the skeptic's answer.** The worker took its key from the driver's de-duplication (`REPORT.md` section 8, decision 5; section 3, "Precedent for row 720").
   - The driver drops an error whose `toString()` it has already seen (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/MultipleStaticError.java:31-39`).
   - That string is the place where the error is reported, followed by its description (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/exceptions/StaticError.java:70-73`).
   - Once an error moves to its call, the reported place is the call's. Two calls then give two strings, and the driver keeps both.
   - The worker's key used `n.at`, the place before the move (`:48` at `a79a51661`). That is the callee's declaration, the wrong place that row 720 repairs. So the worker's key was not the driver's key. It carried the base's wrong place into the de-duplication.

3. **A printed name does not identify a type variable across declarations.**
   - With the worker's key, whether `second`'s call is reported depends on whether `second` calls its parameter `T` or `U` (`SkTwoCalls` against `SkTwoCallsU`, above).
   - The tree's own test of the same principle, for bound checks, is `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/BoundCheckSameNameTwoScopes.fss:1` and `:11-12`: "the same question about T has two answers". That test is the revival's (`3c67d5204`), not the team's.

4. **The fix meets each of the worker's concerns.**
   - *A call inside a tuple was counted twice in the first version* (`REPORT.md` section 1, "The first (96c441771)"). The call's place lies inside the tuple's, so only the call's place is kept (`:50-56`). `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce` now asserts two errors: one at the call in the tuple, at `:13:21-`, and `again`'s own. It does not assert three.
   - *A type that is ill-formed where it is written was counted twice in the second version.* `written` suppresses every moved place of that key (`:44`, `:72-74`). `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce.test` still asserts 'has 1 error'.
   - *A type built twice from one declaration* (decision 5's way not taken). One call's own expressions nest or coincide. Nested places keep the inner one. Coinciding places print the same string, which the driver drops (`MultipleStaticError.java:34-37`).
   - *A call's value that flows to a later use.* The use shares the call's node, so it adds no place (`:79-85`). Fix 5.1 makes the walk meet the call first (`:286-287`, upheld as settled in `SKEPTIC.md` 5.1).
   - The skeptic's runs on `491a5631a`: the rung's 35 test files, 'OK (47 tests)'; `ant testQuick`, 'Tests run: 1222, Failures: 0, Errors: 0', 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL' (`SKEPTIC.md` sections 5.2 and 11).

5. **The library's sites hold by reading.**
   - The rung's section says that row 720's repair "moves two sites without adding one" (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, rung K, "Distance sites").
   - `MaxSumReductionPair` and `MinSumReductionPair` appear in `Library/` only at their declarations (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3405`, `:3411`) and at one call each (`:3422`, `:3424`). So each moved key has one place, and the fix gives one error for each, as the worker's code did.
   - The skeptic's instrumented runs agree on the tables' api rows and on the two moved sites (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Row 488").

## 4. Each side's claims

**The worker was right that:**
- the first version multiplied errors (`REPORT.md` section 1);
- the driver de-duplicates on text and place (`MultipleStaticError.java:31-39`);
- a key on node identity alone would double one call's type wherever it is built twice. The skeptic agrees, and that is why the nesting rule exists (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Mine").

**The worker was wrong that** "each of the base's distinct errors stays one error" is a requirement. No decision on record asks for the base's count of errors outside the library.
- The base's single error for two calls came from its wrong place (point 2 above).
- `GenTest5` rises from 32 to 36 errors, at three of the four `cross` calls (`:646` to `:648`; the first, at `:645`, was reported already) and at a second reference at `:384`, with its first error unchanged (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, "Its cost"). Each new error is a call that call 4 asks to be reported. `GenTest5` is outside the suites (`ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/`).

**The skeptic was right** about the defect, its dependence on another declaration's parameter name, and call 4's reading (points 1 to 3 above).

**The skeptic measured less than it implied.** Three things in section 5 below are not measured on the committed fix. None changes the ruling.

## 5. What lands unmeasured or unrepaired: for the gather and the curator

1. **No count stage or distance stage ran on `491a5631a`** (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2 and 11).
   - The skeptic's instrumented count run with this code lost row 488's site at `FortressLibrary.fss:130` ('#total 38', '#locations 37'). The worker's file, compiled the same way, did not.
   - The mechanism was not found. The symptom is the one F-232 records: two instrumented runs that shifted the JVM's identity-hash sequence lost `:130` (`explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:282-283`, `:350`).
   - Rung H makes the checker's output the same under any identity-hash sequence. Call 3 names `:130` going or staying as H's own cost (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, call 3).
   - So the gate on the merged tree is the first measure of this fix. If the gate's count or distance moves at any site other than `:130` and the two moved sites `:3422` and `:3424`, the gather looks at `491a5631a` first.
   - `record.md:22` ("In the library no error is added or dropped: the count stays 39 and the distance 49") holds for this fix by reading only (point 5 above). The gather takes the numbers from the gate.
2. **P-148's time for this fix is not measured.**
   - The walk is 0.7 % of the count stage's samples (`REPORT.md:148-149`).
   - The fix adds a linear scan for each moved error (`:80`), and a scan over each key's places at the end (`:45-56`). In the library each key has one place (point 5 above).
   - The gate's count stage times the merged tree.
3. **A line of `record.md` is stale.** The handover line "A call's ill-formed type is reported at the call, once." (`record.md:53`) should read "once for each call", as `record.md:19` and `:32` already do. This is the gather's correction.
4. **A residual case, found by reading and not reproduced.**
   - Take two calls of one callee whose static arguments print alike, where one call is an argument of the other, such as `next[\T\](next[\T\](x))` with a bounded `next`. Both calls' types have one key. The inner call's place lies inside the outer's, so the outer call gives no error (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:50-56`).
   - This case is narrower than the defect fixed, and it does not depend on any other declaration. The program is still refused, at the inner call.
   - The worker's way (e) closes it in general: a call's type takes the call's spans (`REPORT.md` section 8, decision 3). It changes the spans that every message prints, so it is not this batch's.
   - If a later rung reproduces the case, it gets a ledger row.

## 6. If call 4 is reversed

Call 4 is the coordinator's, listed for the curator's review and reversible (`CLIMB-BATCH-16.md`, "The coordinator's calls this batch builds"). If the curator reads "at the call" as "once per callee", `git revert 491a5631a` removes the fix together with its test, the rekey and its lines of `record.md`. The dropped call then needs a ledger row at home 3, with `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce.test` as its reproducer (`SKEPTIC.md` 5.2, last paragraph).

Why: the revival honors the designers' intent and does not change Fortress's nature for a convenience; other languages are consulted only to reconcile a conflict between earlier and later designers' choices, and here there is none. - P-148 **The checker's speed comes right after its correctness.** A rung that changes the checker measures how the change affects the time that the checker needs. First the rung makes the change correct. Then it does a second pass that makes the checker faster. This pass must not change the checker's results: the checker accepts and refuses the same programs as before, with the same errors at the same places. The rung's skeptic checks the time and the results. This work is part of the rung, not a separate step after the landing. #!/bin/bash
# seed-worktree.sh <base-worktree> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]
#
# Makes a worktree that is ready to compile and run Fortress without building anything, by copying the
# build and the caches of a baseline worktree that has been built once, and translating the parts of the
# caches that are keyed by the source tree's absolute path (explorations/coordinator/build-cache-exploration.md).
#
#   <base-worktree>  a clean worktree of this repository at some commit B, on which `ant compileAll` and the
#                    library-order recompile (explorations/repo-internals.md, "Compile order matters") have
#                    run, and nothing since.
#   <new-worktree>   where the new worktree goes; made by `git worktree add`, reused if it already exists.
#   <branch>         the branch it checks out: an existing local branch, else origin's, else a new branch
#                    cut from <start-point>, which defaults to B; `-` makes a detached worktree at
#                    <start-point> instead. Old-against-new runs need no copy of the base: tools/old-fortress.sh
#                    runs the base build itself with a private caches folder.
#
# What it does, in order: adds the worktree; copies ProjectFortress/build, ProjectFortress/.dependencies
# and default_repository/caches from the base; renames every file of the AST caches (analyzed_cache,
# interpreter_cache, interpreter_parsed_cache) to the hash of its source's new path (NamingCzar.deCaseName,
# compiler/NamingCzar.java:244-245; GraphNode.java:33 hashes the canonical path) and rewrites the base path
# inside it; rewrites the base path in the bytecode-cache jars' SourceFile attributes (debug information
# only: jars copied unchanged also run, but their stack traces would name the base's files); and makes the
# new worktree the base's replica in its file dates too. The copies keep the base's dates (cp -a), every
# tracked file whose content is the base's takes the base file's date, and every tracked file that differs
# from B, committed or not, is stamped later than everything copied. Dates decide three things. The
# repository uses a cached entry only when it is not older than its source (repository/GraphRepository.java:244,
# :283; a changed api also makes everything that imports it stale, :600-620). Ant regenerates the AST
# nodes, the parsers and Operators.java when an input is newer than the generated file (build.xml:371-384,
# :450-467, :1335-1400); the checkout's own dates make it regenerate them, and javac then recompiles 1,077
# files. And javac recompiles a source newer than its class (build-cache-exploration.md, section 6). So the
# next `fortress compile` of a differing library source rebuilds it, and a worktree whose ProjectFortress/src
# differs from B is seeded with a warning: the copied build is B's, so the worker runs ant compileAll, which
# recompiles the differing sources (and deletes the caches, build.xml:715 and :356), and the library-order
# recompile before its first compiled run. The base's own dates must be a build's: a base built in place by
# ant, or seeded by this script.
#
# A worktree that already has ProjectFortress/build is left alone (a relaunch keeps the worker's own build);
# SEED_FORCE=1 replaces its build and caches with the base's.
#
# Prints one line per step with its time, and the seeded worktree's path last. Exits non-zero, having

content.content:
- F-220 **`__bigOperator`'s local `body` is typed `body(i: I): L`, which walk runs since it no longer instantiates a big operator's static parameter at `BottomType`.** The checker count passes it (F-53). Gated by `tests/UnwrittenListMapComprehensionWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` section 6.
- F-221 **The compiled checker retries a call written as another call's argument against each enclosing declaration's parameter type, where the enclosing call is not accepted otherwise.** It builds P-51 under P-49, so a declaration that accepts the call as written is never passed over. A reduction's plain-bounded big operator, an argument of `__bigOperator` once desugared, so takes the reduction's expected type; an F-bounded one is still refused (row 731). A chain `a OPLUS b OPLUS c` that only the retry makes acceptable to a multifix declaration now runs it, not the binary one. Walk gives such an argument no expected type (row 705). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCallArgument*` and `InferBigOperatorExpectedType`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-argument-context/REPORT.md` sections 1, 5 and 8, and `SKEPTIC.md` finding 5.
- F-225 **The compiled checker types `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type, read from the trait's F-bound, keeps the signatures plain, and refuses an extender at another type.** It builds P-146. The library's 29 self-typed bodies check. Walk loads what the rule refuses. A compiled body that returns `self` fails verification when the parameter is an object type (row 695). The rule refuses the team demo `trips.fss`'s `generator` (row 710) and `PureList`'s `List` (row 355). Gated by `compiler_tests/SelfType*` and `XXXSelfType*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-self-type/REPORT.md` sections 1, 2, 4 and 7.
- F-226 **The compiled checker renames an inherited method's own static parameters apart before it uses them: from its trait's in the overloading check, and from the receiver's static arguments at a call.** So `Generator.generate[\R\]`, inherited by `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, keeps its own `R` (row 561). At a call, each method that `commonInheritedMethods` returns is instantiated with those of its own static parameters whose names the arguments mention renamed to `name$i`, so a method invocation and a call by name inside a trait are repaired alike. Gated by `compiler_tests/InheritedMethodStaticParamSameName`, `InheritedMethodByNameStaticParamSameName` and `MethodStaticArgReceiverSameName`. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/triage.md` section 3; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-contexts/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-227 **The compiled checker keeps an intersection that names a type or inference variable as written, and reads a variable below a union through the union whole or its bound.** A closed trait is expanded into its listed types only against a conjunct that names no variable (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:708-735`, `:165-180`). So a call through a parameter bounded by a closed trait and a bound excluding a listed type checks, and the Return Type Rule beside it (rows 686, 687, 689, 690 and 711). A `Box[\T\]` argument under a ground second bound stays refused (row 712), and an overloading the base accepted through the expansion is refused (row 713). Gated by `compiler_tests/*TwoBoundsClosedTrait` and `*TwoGroundBounds*ClosedTrait`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6.
- F-231 **The generated AST walker is split into methods that the JVM compiles; as one method it ran interpreted and set the checker's time.** `Walker.walk`, which `ScalaAstGenerator` writes into `FortressAst.scala`, was one method of 31,704 bytes, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit, and the checker's substitutions and normalizations all go through it. Split in order into eight methods, with identical output, the count stage with row 680's repair takes about 340 s on an idle machine instead of 911 s, and the distance stage 931 s instead of 2,375 s. What remains is about 95 % the solver normalizing meets again. Gated by `WalkerJUTest`. Detail: `perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 6.
- F-232 **The checker's output depends on the JVM's identity-hash sequence.** Every AST node's hash starts from its class's identity hash, so the order of every hash map and set of nodes, the apis that `StaticChecker.checkApis` takes in turn among them, moves when any code asks for an identity hash at another moment. One extra identity hash at start reorders the api checks and prints a union's members the other way; two instrumented runs lost row 488's site at `:130`. It is a lead for row 488's moves. Detail: `perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md` section 9.
- F-233 **The compiled checker types a block's local functions with their group in scope.** So a local function with no written return type whose body calls another member of its group, as `Array3`'s `asString` does, checks; one that calls itself is refused for its reference cycle, as a top-level function is. Gated by `compiler_tests/LocalFunctionSiblingInLoop`, `LocalFunctionSiblingCall` and `XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` section 6.

content.content:
# Running tests

**track**
: One of the four JVMs of `ant testFast`.

**shard**
: One of the four JVMs of `ant testSystem`. Shard i of n takes every n-th file of the sorted list, from index i.

**code state**
: Code of a tree as one edit leaves it. Only an edit of code makes a new code state; a commit does not.

## The two suites

`ant testFast` runs about 1,800 tests in four tracks at once, in about 9 to 11 minutes:

- compiler: `CompilerJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/` and `parser_tests/`. It is the longest track, so it sets the total time.
- library: `LibraryJUTest` over `library_tests/`.
- othercompiler: `OtherCompilerJUTest` over `other_compiler_tests/`.
- misc: the unit `*JUTest` classes.

`ant testSystem` runs `SystemJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, the interpreter's test folder. It runs about 500 tests in four shards, in about 2 to 4 minutes.

`ant testSpecData` runs the specification's 130 extracted examples (`SpecData/examples/basic`, `preliminaries`, `advanced`) under walk, in under a minute. The gate runs it after the two suites.

The newest gate summary has the exact counts and times of the last landed run:

    git log -1 --name-only --format= -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt'

The two suites work in the same way:

- Each suite runs `ant compileAll` first, as every `ant` test target does, so it never tests stale classes. After an edit of Java or Scala, that build empties `default_repository/caches` (`build-and-caches.md`, "Building"). Each analyses or compiles the Fortress code that it tests, in private caches.
- Each JVM gets 768 MB, a 32 MB stack and `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, whatever the shell exports. The run steps of the compiled tests get `JAVA_FLAGS=-Xmx4g -Xss64m`, also whatever the shell exports.
- Each suite deletes `ProjectFortress/test-caches` when it starts. Each JVM keeps its caches in a folder of its own under it, so that the JVMs do not overwrite each other's entries. Temporary files go to `ProjectFortress/test-tmp/`.
- The results are in `ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/fast-<track>/` and `system-<i>/`, as `TEST-<class>.txt`.

To run a suite:

- Run one suite at a time in a tree, because each suite deletes the `test-caches` that the other uses.
- Read the verdict in the line before `Total time:`: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` means zero failures, and `BUILD FAILED` means at least one. Every `ant` test target ends with these lines, and exits non-zero when it failed.
- To compare test counts, compare the sum of the four shards. A file added to `tests/` moves every later file to another shard.
- If a suite's count fell, a `.test` file or a `tests=` line almost always went missing.

## The switches that the harness reads

Put a `-D` switch on the `java` line of a run by hand; the `java` line in `harness-one.sh` is a model. On the `ant` line, it does not reach the suites' JVMs.

- `-Dtests=<dir>`: the folder that `SystemJUTest` runs, in place of `tests/`.
- `-Dfortress.suite.shard=i/n`: run shard i of n only.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.count=N`: run N files at most.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.seed=<value>`: the order of the files. Each run prints its seed as `FORTRESS_UNITTESTS_SEED=...`.
- `FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1` for `SystemJUTest`, `-Dfortress.junit.verbose=true` for the compiled tests' classes: show the output of passing tests too.
- `-Dfortress.junit.reset=false`: `CompilerJUTest` and `LibraryJUTest` keep their caches folder. Without it, they empty it when they start.

## Outside the gate

- `ant testNotPassing` runs the interpreter programs of `ProjectFortress/not_passing_yet/`, which are expected to fail. It fails if one of them passes.
- Nothing runs these folders: `not_working_compiler_tests/`, `not_working_library_tests/`, `not_working_static_tests/`, `obsolete_interpreter_tests/`, `long_term_not_working/`, `linker_tests/`, `compiler_regressions/`. Put every new test in a gated test folder. A test of a defect that fails today is an `XXX` test there (`tests-writing.md`).

## When to run a whole suite

- The gate runs every suite once, on the tree that lands (`gate.md`). Your brief says whether you run the gate.
- If your edit changes the Java or Scala of the checker, of walk or of a phase that both paths share, run all the tests that it reaches. Run them once, after your last edit of code. The run needs no commit.
  - For the checker, run `ant testQuick`: the compiler, othercompiler and library tracks at once (below).
  - For walk, run `ant testSystem`. It is the same as its four shards run by hand.
  - For a shared phase (under `compiler/`: name binding, DSL grammars, desugaring, the marking of overloaded calls in `OverloadRewriter`) or the parser, run both.
- Quote the verdict lines and the command in your report, with the commit if your code is committed.
- If the gate later runs on a tree that holds other changes too, that tree is another code state. Your run and the gate's run do not repeat each other.
- After an edit of the code generator (`codegen/`, `OverloadSet`) or the run time (`runtimeSystem/`), run your own tests, and the four-thread atomic runs (`gate.md`) if `compiler.md` asks for them. Leave the whole tracks to the gate.
- After every other change, run only your own tests, through the scripts below. Leave the rest to the gate. This includes an edit of either library, though it reaches many tests.

The suites do not check these:

- the bytecode optimizer, which nothing in the compiler calls;
- DSL grammars, except one program whose phases the misc track runs: `syntax_abstraction_tests/ForUse.fss`;
- the linker's aliasing of apis;
- `fortress unparse`;
- the round trip of the `.tfi` and `.tfs` caches;
- a behaviour above one thread that one run of each suite at four threads does not hit.

If your edit is in one of these, your own tests are its only check. Say so in your report.

## One test, or a few

Each script and `fortress junit` below ends with the verdict of JUnit's text runner: `OK (n tests)`, or `FAILURES!!!` with the counts. Read the verdict there: the exit code is 0 whatever the verdict.

### Interpreter tests

Run interpreter tests (`ProjectFortress/tests/`) from the tree's root, after you set up the call:

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh <tree>/tmp/h1 \
        ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss [ProjectFortress/tests/X.test] [more files ...]

- It runs `SystemJUTest` with testSystem's JVM settings, at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, on a folder that holds only the files that you name.
- It keeps its cache in the folder `<scratch-dir>.cache`. It starts from that cache while the build and the library sources are those that filled it. Otherwise, or with `COLD_CACHE=1`, it starts empty. Its first line says `cache filled` or `cache empty`.
- It runs the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/` and builds nothing. After you edit Java, Scala or a parser grammar, run `ant compileAll` first. If your tree has no build, seed it or build it as `worktrees.md` says.
- Give it a scratch directory that holds nothing else. The script deletes the directory when it starts and when it ends.
- If a test has an `X.test` file (its keys for a refusal at load), name it beside its `X.fss`.
- It takes 15 to 25 s with an empty cache, mostly to analyse the library, and about 4 s with a filled one. Name several files in one call to run them in one JVM.
- It shows the output of passing tests too, and removes the Java stack frames.
